Screen checkConfirm in Vanderbilt's Oracle or UKG during a recorded demo: where Costing for Persons sits in Redwood; the Advanced Search and Effective As-of Date labels; the Actions, Create, and Edit menu labels; whether Oracle fills in the account for a COA string; that a regular HCM (not a super-user) sees Our Workforce and this quick action.

1 · Intro

When to use it.

Use Costing for Persons to enter or change where an assignment, or a single pay element, is charged. You need the HCM role in Oracle to enter costing; a FUM can't unless they have that role too.

Get the COA or POET string from your FUM before you start. Costing for an assignment and costing for an element are different tasks.

Use this whenThe default won't work and a person or a payment needs specific costing, or existing costing needs to start differently, be fixed, stop, or be removed.

Follow along in Oracle HCM. Check off each step as you go.

Before you submit

The same four checks on every pay-impacting transaction. Draft: the owner for this area confirms anything marked To confirm.

Attach

  • Prior periods: the Retro Costing Request Form (Salary), sent to the Research Finance Team Required
  • Cost transfer memo, if an externally funded grant is affected Required

Check

Read every field back against the source document: person, effective date, position, hours, pay, and costing.

  • Effective As-of Date is the first day of the pay period the costing should start.
  • The lines total 100%.
  • The COA or POET string came from your finance partner.
  • You ran the HCM Cost Allocation Verification Plan report afterward.

To confirmWhere the Retro Change Cutoff is published. It is not on the HR/Payroll Calendar.

Cutoff

Current and future changes: enter by the HCM Transaction Cutoff. Prior periods: send the Retro Costing Request Form (Salary) to the Research Finance Team by the Retro Change Cutoff, usually two business days earlier.

Who does what

  • Who starts it: You. Entering costing needs the HCM role in Oracle; get the costing string from your FUM.
  • Who approves: To confirm: the approval chain for this transaction.
  • What happens next: Oracle uses the costing in effect on the Pay Period End Date and does not prorate.

Watch-outs

  • Costing applies to a full pay period. Oracle uses the costing in effect on the Pay Period End Date and does not prorate.
  • Current and future changes: enter by the HCM Transaction Cutoff.
  • Prior periods: also submit the Retro Costing Request Form (Salary) to the Research Finance Team by the Retro Change Cutoff, usually two business days before the HCM Transaction Cutoff. Include a cost transfer memo if an externally funded grant is affected.
  • Don't End Date a prior period if you want to keep costing records that come after that date. End Date ends everything from that date forward. After End Date, use Create, not Update, to add costing again.
  • Open item: confirm whether Oracle fills in the account for a COA string on an assignment.
  • Open item: confirm whether the Retro Costing Request Form is the retro cost transfer (RCT) form, and its criteria.
  • Open item: bring back the costing visual from the Oracle implementation, updated.

HCM Academy job aid · Costing Management

Enter costing for a person

Use when: The default won't work and a person or a payment needs specific costing, or existing costing needs to start differently, be fixed, stop, or be removed. · System: Oracle HCM (Costing for Persons)

  1. Open Costing for Persons.
  2. Search the person with Advanced Search and the right Effective As-of Date.
    • Use the Pay Period Begin Date (from the payroll calendar) of the period the costing should start.
    • A future-dated change: enter that future date.
    • End Date: search on the last day of the last pay period the costing should apply.
    • Prior pay periods also need the retro form; see the watch-outs.
  3. Select the person, then review the costing History.
  4. Cost the assignment.
  5. Cost an element.
  6. Change existing costing with Edit.
  7. Enter each costing line. Percentages must total 100%.
    • Whole percentages are recommended; decimals are allowed, for example for grant cost share.
    • COA string: Entity, Net Asset Class (for example, 05), Financial Unit, Program and Activity (000 if unused), VU_Function. Use default zeros for InterEntity (000), Future 2 (0), and the POET fields (0000). Leave Allocation Type blank.
    • Account: for an element, enter it: 5110 faculty, 5120 staff, 5130 student.
    • POET string (grants and projects): in the COA fields, enter the payroll clearing string 380.05.38600.5140.000.000.000.VUI.0, then Project Number, Organization, Expenditure Type (SalFac, SalStaff, or SalStud), and Task. Leave Allocation Type blank.
  8. Select Submit.
  9. Run the Cost Allocation Verification report.

  • Check: Effective As-of Date is the first day of the pay period the costing should start. The lines total 100%. The COA or POET string came from your finance partner. You ran the HCM Cost Allocation Verification Plan report afterward.
  • Cutoff: By the HCM Transaction Cutoff. Prior periods: the retro form by the Retro Change Cutoff, usually two business days earlier.

  • Costing applies to a full pay period. Oracle uses the costing in effect on the Pay Period End Date and does not prorate.
  • Current and future changes: enter by the HCM Transaction Cutoff.
  • Prior periods: also submit the Retro Costing Request Form (Salary) to the Research Finance Team by the Retro Change Cutoff, usually two business days before the HCM Transaction Cutoff. Include a cost transfer memo if an externally funded grant is affected.
